hero.intro: IITG-TIC is the Technology Incubation Centre of IIT Guwahati — a home for researchers, students and founders to turn early-stage ideas into businesses worth backing. We pair entrepreneurs with multidisciplinary mentors, run technical and business support, and lower the risk around an idea so it can grow into a venture that stands on its own.

posts.title: Deep tech in the North-East
posts.sliderTagline: Three founders, one evening, hard questions.
posts.excerpt: An evening with three founders building hardware ventures across Guwahati and Shillong — how they raised, who they shipped to, what they got wrong.
posts.author: Hosted by IITG-TIC

coverImage.alt: A previous edition of the speaker series at the centre.

body.text: We're hosting three founders for an evening conversation about building hardware ventures in the North-East. The session is informal, the questions land where the audience takes them, and the answers are not curated.

Confirmed: a robotics founder shipping field equipment to tea estates, a sensor company that landed its first defence contract last quarter, and a battery startup that pivoted twice before product-market fit.

body.caption: A previous edition of the series, March 2026.

body.text: Schedule
6:30pm — arrivals and tea. 7:00pm — talks (twenty minutes each, plus questions). 8:30pm — open conversation. 9:30pm — close.
Who should attend
Current cohort, applicants thinking through their next year, partners and mentors. Outside founders welcome — please RSVP so we can plan seating.

posts.title: Cohort showcase: Q2 2026
posts.sliderTagline: Quarterly cohort review, held in public.
posts.excerpt: The current cohort presents what they've shipped this quarter — open to mentors, partners and invited investors. Followed by an open Q&A.
posts.author: Programme team

body.text: Once a quarter, the current cohort presents what they've shipped — to mentors, partners, and a small set of invited investors. It's not a pitch competition; it's a working review held in public.
Each team gets fifteen minutes — ten to show what they built, five for questions. We keep the questions hard and the audience small enough that real answers can land.

body.caption: Q1 2026 showcase — four teams, two hundred attendees.

body.text: Agenda
10:00am — opening remarks. 10:30am — team presentations. 1:00pm — lunch and informal exchange. 2:30pm — Q&A panel. 4:00pm — close.
Attending
Mentors and partners receive invitations automatically. Investors and outside guests by curated invitation. If you'd like to attend, write to us — we keep the room small but the door isn't closed.

posts.title: IDE Bootcamp 2026
posts.excerpt: Five days of design thinking, business development, financial planning and pitch prep — 150 student innovators from 27 institutions across 14 states.
posts.author: IITG-TIC with SART, MoE Innovation Cell and AICTE

coverImage.alt: Participants at the IDE Bootcamp finale.

body.text: The Innovation, Design and Entrepreneurship Bootcamp ran from 20 to 24 April 2026 — five immersive days organised by IITG-TIC together with the School of Agro and Rural Technology (SART), with support from the Ministry of Education's Innovation Cell and AICTE.

Nearly 150 student innovators travelled from 27 institutions across 14 states. The format was action-packed by design — design thinking sessions in the morning, startup business development through the afternoon, financial planning and pitch preparation in the evenings.

body.caption: A working session inside the centre on day two.

body.text: What participants did

Beyond the lecture content, participants spent time inside the IITG-TIC facility and the BioNest Incubator — real labs, real benches, real founders walking through. The bootcamp closed with a competitive product-pitching finale, judged by a panel of startup and industry experts.
Outcome

A handful of teams left with concrete next steps — applications into the next cohort, mentor connections, and in two cases, early customer conversations. The bootcamp is now an annual fixture in the centre's calendar.

posts.title: Seminar series on startups & entrepreneurship
posts.sliderTagline: Weekly Friday sessions with guest experts.
posts.excerpt: Launched May 2025 — a weekly online seminar series for early-stage startups, researchers and student entrepreneurs. Every Friday, guided by guest experts.
posts.author: Hosted by IITG-TIC

coverImage.alt: A speaker delivering a seminar session over Zoom.

body.text: Launched in May 2025, the IITG-TIC seminar series is a weekly online knowledge-sharing initiative for early-stage startups, researchers and budding student entrepreneurs. Sessions run every Friday over Zoom.

Each week brings a different guest expert — legal professionals, chartered accountants, venture capital investors, veteran founders. The roster is chosen to cover the operating questions founders actually run into, rather than the inspirational territory.

body.alt: A guest speaker mid-session over Zoom.
body.caption: A recent Friday session with a venture investor.

body.text: What gets covered

The sessions are structured around the real startup milestones — ideation and business modeling, navigating intellectual property rights and legal compliances, leveraging available government schemes, and pitching to investors.
How to attend
Open to founders, researchers and students. Register through the contact form on the apply page to be added to the weekly invitation list.

posts.title: AquaTech Innovators Hackathon 2025
posts.excerpt: A 5-day hackathon focused on underwater robotics — undergraduate and postgraduate engineers designing autonomous underwater vehicles for marine exploration.
posts.author: IITG-TIC with IITG TIDF

coverImage.alt: An AUV prototype being tested during the hackathon.

body.text: Organised in collaboration with the IIT Guwahati Technology Innovation Hub (IITG TIDF), the AquaTech Innovators Hackathon ran from 17 to 21 March 2025 — five days dedicated to pioneering the future of underwater robotics.

The event drew undergraduate and postgraduate engineering students from across the country. The challenge: design and develop autonomous underwater vehicles capable of tackling real-world marine exploration problems.

body.alt: Hackathon team working on an AUV.
body.caption: A team during the fabrication phase of the hackathon.

body.text: What was on offer
Hands-on fabrication workshops, expert mentorship and access to the centre's specialised facilities — the Mechatronics Lab and 3D Printing Lab — all available for the full five days.
Rewards
Top teams earned cash rewards and were offered incubation and funding pathways up to ₹5 lakhs through IITG-TIC. Several of those teams went on to formal incubation enquiries in the following months.

posts.title: Agri-startup financing and agritech innovation
posts.excerpt: A joint programme with Assam Startup, NABARD and BIRD — focused on scaling agritech ventures across the North-East.
posts.author: IITG-TIC with Assam Startup, NABARD and BIRD

coverImage.alt: Agritech founders at the financing workshop.

body.text: IITG-TIC has co-organised specialised programmes focused on scaling agritech startups across the North-East. The most prominent of these — a joint foundational programme held with Assam Startup, the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), and the Banking Institute of Rural Development (BIRD).

The programme was built for modern agritech founders. The content sat squarely on the practical side — financial planning, securing credit lines, navigating agricultural subsidies, and deploying smart-farming solutions in the regional context.

body.alt: A working session at the agritech programme.
body.caption: A financing workshop in session with NABARD facilitators.

body.text: Why this matters here

The region's economy remains heavily agrarian. Scaling agritech ventures locally has knock-on effects far beyond the founders themselves — better tooling for small holders, better routes to market, and a viable career path for engineers from the region who want to stay.
What founders left with

Concrete next steps on credit lines, subsidy applications and pilot deployments — and an introduction into the wider agritech network that the centre has built across the North-East over the last several years.

posts.title: Samsung's 'Solve for Tomorrow' roadshow
posts.excerpt: The Guwahati leg of Samsung India's national 'Solve for Tomorrow' roadshow — over 100 participants pitching tech-driven solutions for environmental challenges.
posts.author: IITG-TIC with Samsung India

coverImage.alt: Solve for Tomorrow roadshow at IIT Guwahati.

body.text: In April 2024, IITG-TIC partnered with Samsung India to host the Guwahati leg of the national 'Solve for Tomorrow' roadshow. The event targeted youth between 18 and 22, with one stated aim — to nurture a culture of innovative problem-solving and environmental sustainability.

Over 100 participants from IIT Guwahati and surrounding institutions took part. The format paired motivational insights from award-winning rocket scientists with working sessions on pitching tech-driven solutions.

body.caption: A team pitching during the Guwahati leg of the roadshow.

body.text: What participants tackled
Three problem areas anchored the day — waste segregation, carbon emission tracking, and water pollution control. Each team picked one and built a pitch over the course of the session.
Why it mattered

The roadshow exposed a younger audience to the centre's facilities and to early-stage product thinking. A few participants returned later for the IDE Bootcamp; one filed an application to the cohort the following year.

posts.title: Defense innovation outreach with iDEX-DIO
posts.sliderTagline: ADITI and DISC opportunities for the NE.
posts.excerpt: Outreach sessions in collaboration with iDEX and the Defence Innovation Organisation — guiding North East Indian innovators toward national defence and aerospace challenges.
posts.author: IITG-TIC with iDEX and DIO

coverImage.alt: A defence outreach session at the centre.

body.text: In early 2024, IITG-TIC organised multiple defence innovation outreach sessions in collaboration with the Innovation for Defence Excellence (iDEX) and the Defence Innovation Organisation (DIO).
The sessions brought together defence experts, technology innovators and startup founders to discuss opportunities under national initiatives — specifically the ADITI and DISC challenge frameworks.

body.alt: A defence outreach session in progress.
body.caption: An iDEX briefing session at the centre.

body.text: Where the focus sat

The technical sessions focused on guiding North East Indian innovators to build deep-tech prototypes for national defence, aerospace and secure communication. The region's specific advantages — proximity to strategic borders, established hardware talent — were threaded through the conversation.
What followed
Several attendees went on to file challenge proposals under iDEX. The centre continues to host targeted outreach as new defence challenges are announced.

hero.intro: At IITG-TIC we don't just give you a desk and walk away. The centre is built around five connected forms of support — infrastructure, programme, technical depth, capital, and a place to live while you build. Each one exists to lower the cost of starting something hard, and shorten the distance between an idea and a paying customer.

links.title: Incubation Support
links.tagline: Launch your tech startup with in-house or digital incubation — workspace, labs, mentorship and a community that holds it together.

hero.lede: IITG-TIC offers two ways to incubate — a fully equipped in-house programme inside our campus, and a digital track for founders who can't be physically here. The support stays the same; the geography is yours to choose.

sections.label: In-house
paragraphs: Move into a fully equipped workstation inside the Technology Complex. Meeting rooms and shared spaces sit across the same building, so collaboration happens naturally rather than as a calendar invite.
Access state-of-the-art labs across electronics, biotechnology, machining and fabrication — the kind of equipment that turns a CAD file into a working prototype on the same week.
High-speed internet, IT infrastructure and the everyday plumbing that lets you focus on the work and forget the logistics.

image.alt: An in-house incubation workstation at the centre.

sections.label: Digital
paragraphs: Receive guidance from experienced mentors remotely, on the same cadence as our in-house cohort. Geography does not change the depth of the engagement.
Benefit from the programme's resources and structure on your own terms — no pressure to relocate, no compromise on what's offered.
Tap into a wider pool of investors and potential partners through our digital network. The door opens the same way; you just walk through it from wherever you are.

image.alt: A digital incubatee in a remote mentorship session.

sections.label: Community
paragraphs: Whether you're in-house or digital, you join a living community of fellow founders, mentors and industry experts. Some of the most valuable conversations happen in the margins of programmed time.

Cohort-wide events, peer reviews and informal exchanges form the connective tissue between incubatees. The community is small enough that everyone knows everyone — and serious enough that the conversations land.

image.alt: A cohort gathering at the centre's community space.

links.title: Infrastructure Support
links.tagline: Office space, shared facilities and access to IIT Guwahati's wider infrastructure — labs, library and expert opinion on call.

hero.lede: Infrastructure at IITG-TIC comes in three layers — your own office setup, shared facilities across the cohort, and access to the wider institute's labs, library and expert advisers when your work needs them.

sections.label: Individual setup
paragraphs: Office space is allocated against requirement — from a single desk to a private team room. Each setup includes a personal computer, internet connection and a working telephone line.
Office furniture is provided. On-campus accommodation is offered subject to availability — see our residence-support page if you'll need it.

image.alt: An allocated office setup at the centre.

sections.label: Shared facilities
paragraphs: A conference room equipped with projection equipment is available for cohort meetings, investor conversations and team workshops.
Shared office hardware — photocopier, fax machine, laser printer and scanner — is at every incubatee's disposal, so the small operational frictions don't become recurring problems.

sections.label: Institute resources
paragraphs: Incubatees can access the institute's wider infrastructure — labs, workshops and the IITG library — per the institute's standard norms.

Expert opinion on legal, financial and technical matters can be arranged from IITG faculty and advisers on a chargeable basis. Medical facilities at the institute are similarly available on chargeable terms.

image.alt: An incubatee using the IITG library.

links.title: Funding Support
links.tagline: Soft loans up to 80% of project cost, navigation across major government schemes, and CSR partnerships with corporates.

hero.lede: Funding at IITG-TIC comes through three connected paths — a soft-loan facility for selected incubatees, navigation help across major government schemes, and CSR partnerships with corporates who fund our work directly.

sections.label: Soft loan
paragraphs: IITG-TIC may offer a soft loan — entirely dependent on the availability of funds, grants and schemes meant for the purpose. We approach government, private and public-sector agencies for grants whenever the opportunity arises.

Soft loans are sanctioned only to registered companies. Admission to IITG-TIC does not automatically entitle a company to a loan, and disbursement follows the guidelines of the underlying funding agency.
The total loan available depends on the funding agency's criteria. As a guideline, soft loans cover up to 80% of project cost — with minimum simple interest where the underlying scheme permits.

sections.label: Government schemes
paragraphs: We help incubatees navigate the major schemes available to early-stage ventures — Startup India, the OIL India Fund and NEDFi Venture among them.
The documentation is half the battle. We've filed many of these before; the programme team will sit with you to assemble a serious application, not a hopeful one.

image.alt: A founder reviewing scheme paperwork at the centre.

sections.label: CSR partnerships
paragraphs: Section 135 of the Companies Act 2013 requires qualifying corporates to spend 2% of average net profits on Corporate Social Responsibility projects. Contributions to technology business incubators located within Central-Government-approved academic institutions qualify under Schedule VII, item (ix).

IITG-TIC is a non-profit technology business incubator hosted at IIT Guwahati since 2009 — one of the first in the North-East — supported by the Technology Development Board (TDB) and the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY). The centre runs across 15,000+ sq ft of infrastructure and has incubated ~19 companies to date.

Corporates can associate with IITG-TIC to implement projects in relevant technology areas, social innovation, or to fund the incubation programme directly. Write to inchargetic@iitg.ac.in or call +91 361 258 3191 to start a conversation.

image.alt: A corporate CSR partnership conversation in progress.

links.title: Technical Support
links.tagline: Labs, workshops and library access — plus faculty mentors and institute-grade testing facilities for product validation.

hero.lede: Our incubatees plug into the full technical depth of IIT Guwahati — the labs and workshops, the faculty who teach in them, and the institute-grade testing facilities that turn a prototype into a credible product.

sections.label: Labs & workshops
paragraphs: Incubatee companies are provided access to the laboratories and workshops of IIT Guwahati per the institute's standard norms — for everything from rapid fabrication to longer R&D cycles.

Mechanical, electronics, materials and embedded labs are routinely accessible. Specialised equipment — clean rooms, characterisation tools, fabrication facilities — is booked through the respective IITG departments based on availability.

image.alt: An incubatee using an IITG lab.

sections.label: Faculty mentors
paragraphs: Our mentors are faculty from IIT Guwahati. They provide full technical support — sitting in on architecture reviews, design reviews and code reviews as engineers, not as evaluators.

Mentor matches are made deliberately. A hardware founder is paired with someone who has built hardware; a software venture with someone who has shipped systems. The fit is the point of the match — not the title.
Beyond scheduled reviews, mentors are reachable for the small judgement calls that don't warrant a meeting but compound across a quarter.

image.alt: An IITG faculty mentor in a technical review.

sections.label: Testing facilities
paragraphs: Testing facilities at IIT Guwahati are available to incubatees — for product validation, performance characterisation, and the quality work that needs equipment beyond an early-stage budget.
Booking and access happen through the institute's standard channels. The programme team helps with introductions and the paperwork the first time you need them.
Use of the institute's library as a reference resource is included — particularly useful for deep-tech ventures that need access to journals, standards and technical literature.

image.alt: An incubatee running a product validation test.

links.title: Residence Support
links.tagline: Shared on-campus hostels inside IIT Guwahati — for founders who need to live close to the centre during a build cycle.

hero.lede: Some incubatees need to be physically close to the centre during a build cycle. Where possible, we offer residential space inside the IITG campus — shared hostels with basic amenities and proximity to the wider institute community.

sections.label: Shared hostels
paragraphs: Based on availability, startup teams are provided residential space with basic amenities in shared hostels on the IITG campus.
Rooms are furnished and utilities are included. Access to campus dining and the library follows the institute's standard norms.
Allocation is per team and per programme stage — not per founder. We aim to keep teams housed together so that the build doesn't lose its rhythm.

image.alt: A shared hostel room on the IITG campus.

sections.label: Campus life
paragraphs: The hostel sits inside the IITG campus, which means our incubatees live next door to the students. Some of the best conversations and recruiting moments happen because of that proximity.
Campus life includes access to dining halls, sports facilities, and academic events — the kind of environment that keeps founders close to fresh ideas and fresh hires.
It is, in practice, the closest thing we offer to building inside a research lab while still running a company.

image.alt: A view of campus life at IIT Guwahati.

sections.label: How to request
paragraphs: If you'll need residence support to join a cohort, mention it in your application — it helps us plan early and gives us time to confirm availability.
If the need arises mid-cohort, raise it with the programme manager. We respond within a week with a real answer — yes or no, with reasoning.

image.alt: A founder filling out a residence request form.

hero.lede: The centre's work is supported by a network across government, industry and academia — each contributing the capital, frameworks or recognition that make our incubation programmes possible.

opportunities.heading: Opportunities
opportunities.title: Opportunities · IITG TIC

hero.intro: Open positions and internships at startups currently being incubated at IITG-TIC. Hiring is small and specific — most teams are under twenty people. If something fits, apply directly to the team.

opportunities.emptyMessage: No open roles right now. Check back in a couple of weeks — the cohort hires in bursts.

posts.description: Designing and iterating on the mechanical platforms behind our tea-estate field robots — chassis, drivetrains and the moving parts that meet the weather. Comfortable on a bench and at a CAD station.
Owning the firmware that runs on our wireless vibration sensors — low-power C on ARM Cortex-M, BLE/LoRa stacks, and the OTA path that keeps deployed units in the field updateable.

Working alongside the BMS team on cell-level characterisation, thermal modelling and the test rigs that prove our packs hold up under field conditions. Open to final-year students and recent graduates.

Building the procurement and distribution backbone — relationships with farmer collectives upstream, logistics into the two national chains we're talking to downstream. Strong fit if you've worked with FPOs or rural supply chains before.
Working on the slide-review assistant that supports pathologists in tier-two hospitals. Experience with vision transformers, weakly-supervised learning or histopathology data is a strong plus.

Owning the pipeline that takes raw sensor data from our municipal deployments and turns it into the dashboards municipalities actually use. Comfortable with Python, time-series stores and the operational side of running a live system.

Tuning the autopilot and control loops on our survey-grade UAVs. PX4/ArduPilot experience is useful but not required — what matters is that you understand the control theory and have shipped a flying platform before.
Designing the small-batch loom-side jigs and software interfaces we ship to weaving cooperatives. Best fit if you can talk to weavers, sketch a fix, and prototype it the same week.

hero.intro: Three views of the cohort — the teams currently inside the centre, the ones we support remotely on our virtual track, and the alumni that have graduated and moved on. Each list is small on purpose; we'd rather work deeply with a few than thinly with many.

categories.title: Current Incubatees
categories.tagline: Teams inside the centre right now — building product, hiring engineers, and shipping to early customers.

hero.lede: These are the ventures currently incubating at IITG-TIC — working from our labs, drawing on our mentor network and shipping to their first cohort of customers. Most are in their first two years.

startups.name: Northeast Robotics
startups.oneLiner: Autonomous field robots for India's tea estates.
startups.description: Building autonomous wheeled platforms that handle plucking and crop-monitoring across the tea estates of Upper Assam. First two pilots running with regional estates; commercial deployment scheduled for late 2026.
startups.problem: Tea plucking is labour-intensive, seasonal, and increasingly hard to staff. Estates lose 8–12% of yield to delayed plucking windows alone.
startups.solution: A rugged, low-ground-pressure wheeled robot that navigates rows of tea bushes, plucks selectively using a vision-guided arm, and uploads field-health telemetry from onboard sensors.
startups.targetMarket: Mid-to-large tea estates across Assam, West Bengal and Tamil Nadu — roughly 1,200 estates above 200 hectares.

mentors: Prof. R. Sharma · IITG, Mechanical Engineering
Anita Bose · Operating Partner, AgFunder India

founders.name: Diganta Kalita
founders.bio: Former robotics engineer at a Bengaluru deeptech firm; grew up in a tea-estate family in Dibrugarh.

founders.name: Priyam Goswami
founders.bio: ML researcher, IITG '21; built the perception stack for an autonomous wheelchair project.

mediaMentions.title: Tea estates turn to homegrown robotics

testimonials.quote: The selective-plucking accuracy beat what we'd seen from imported systems at three times the price.
testimonials.author: Estate manager

milestones.event: First field prototype deployed on partner estate

startups.impactCreated: 180 ha under robotic surveillance; ~25 estate jobs upskilled from plucking to robot supervision.

startups.name: Sensora Labs
startups.tagline: Low-cost vibration sensors for legacy machinery.
startups.oneLiner: Wireless retrofit sensors that give old machines a voice.
startups.description: Retrofit vibration and temperature sensors for older industrial machines — wireless, battery-powered, with a backend that flags failure signatures weeks in advance. Currently piloting with two cement plants in the region.
startups.problem: Most legacy industrial plants in India run machines built before 2010 — no telemetry, no condition monitoring. Unplanned downtime costs the average cement plant ₹4–6 Cr per year.
startups.solution: A battery-powered wireless sensor that clamps onto any motor or pump in minutes, paired with a backend that learns each machine's failure signature.
features: 3-year battery life on a single cell
On-prem dashboard option for air-gapped plants
startups.targetMarket: Mid-tier process manufacturers — cement, paper, steel re-rolling — roughly 8,000 plants nationwide.

founders.name: Manash Bordoloi
founders.bio: Electronics engineer; spent four years on factory-floor automation projects in Pune.

mediaMentions.title: How a Guwahati startup is wiring up India's old factories

testimonials.quote: Two months in, they flagged a bearing failure on a kiln motor that would have cost us a four-day shutdown.
testimonials.author: Plant Head

milestones.event: First sensor v0 deployed in plant pilot

startups.impactCreated: Estimated ₹1.8 Cr in avoided downtime across partner plants in the first 9 months.

startups.name: Voltaic Cells
startups.tagline: Battery packs built for Indian climate conditions.
startups.oneLiner: Lithium-ion packs tuned for high-humidity, high-heat operation.
startups.description: Designing lithium-ion packs that hold up under the temperature and humidity ranges of the North-East. Two product lines in development — one for e-rickshaws, one for telecom backup. First batch ships Q3 2026.
startups.problem: Standard imported battery packs degrade 30–40% faster in NE-India humidity and monsoon-heat cycles than their datasheet suggests.
startups.solution: Climate-tuned BMS, conformal-coated cell stacks and a thermal architecture validated against monsoon-cycle stress tests.
startups.targetMarket: E-rickshaw OEMs in Eastern India, plus telecom tower operators across Tier-2/3 NE locations.

mentors: Prof. S. Dutta · IITG, Electrical Engineering

founders.name: Aniket Borah
founders.bio: Energy-systems engineer; previously at a Hyderabad EV powertrain startup.

startups.name: Millet Labs
startups.tagline: Shelf-stable millet products for urban markets.
startups.oneLiner: Ready-to-cook millet from NE-India farmer collectives.
startups.description: Building a small range of ready-to-cook millet products sourced from farmer collectives across Assam and Meghalaya. Two SKUs in market trial, distribution conversations in progress with two national chains.
startups.problem: Indian urban consumers want healthier carbs but find millet hard to cook and inconsistent in quality.
startups.solution: Pre-processed, ready-in-12-minute millet meals sourced directly from women-led farmer collectives in Assam and Meghalaya.
startups.targetMarket: Health-conscious urban households across Tier-1 Indian cities; ~38M households addressable.

categories.title: Virtual Incubatees
categories.tagline: Founders we support remotely — same depth of engagement, none of the relocation.

hero.lede: Teams on the virtual track work with the same mentors, the same programme structure and the same investor network as our in-house cohort — they just do it from wherever they are. The depth of engagement does not change with geography.

startups.name: Aqua Monitor
startups.tagline: Real-time water-quality sensors for municipal supply.
startups.oneLiner: Continuous drinking-water monitoring for municipal utilities.
startups.description: Building deployed sensor networks that monitor drinking-water quality at the municipal level. Two pilots running in Meghalaya and one in Mizoram. Team operates from Shillong; works with our mentors over weekly remote sessions.
startups.problem: Municipal water boards in NE India rely on weekly manual sampling — contamination events are detected days late.
startups.solution: Low-power probe arrays measure pH, turbidity, residual chlorine and conductivity every 60 seconds, with SMS alerts to ward engineers.
startups.targetMarket: Municipal water utilities across NE India (~120 ULBs).

founders.name: Banlam Marbaniang
founders.bio: Environmental engineer; built water-quality dashboards for the Meghalaya PHED.

achievements: Selected · Atal Community Innovation Centre cohort 2024
startups.impactCreated: ~85,000 residents on continuously-monitored water supply across pilot wards.

startups.name: Weave Tech
startups.tagline: Digital tools for the regional weaving industry.
startups.oneLiner: Software and small-batch automation for handloom cooperatives.
startups.description: Software and small-batch automation tools for traditional weaving cooperatives across Nagaland. The team prefers to stay close to their workshops — the virtual track lets them keep that proximity while drawing on our network.
startups.problem: Traditional Naga weavers spend 40% of their time on order management, dye-batch tracking and inventory — work that pulls them off the loom.
startups.solution: A mobile-first cooperative OS in Nagamese/English that handles orders, dye batches, payouts and design libraries.
startups.targetMarket: ~600 registered weaving cooperatives across Nagaland, Mizoram and Manipur.

founders.name: Imnatoshi Aier
founders.bio: Daughter of a master weaver; software engineer by training.

startups.name: PathLab AI
startups.oneLiner: Slide-review assistance for pathologists in smaller hospitals.
startups.description: Building a diagnostic-imaging assistant that helps pathologists in smaller hospitals review slides faster. Two pilot deployments in Manipur and one in Tripura. Team operates from Imphal with remote programme support.
startups.problem: Tier-2 and tier-3 hospitals across NE India often have one pathologist serving 60+ slides a day. Turnaround is slow and error rates rise toward the end of the shift.
startups.solution: An AI assistant that pre-screens digitised slides, flags candidate regions of interest, and ranks them by likelihood — letting the pathologist work top-down.

hero.lede: The questions we hear most often from founders, applicants and partners — and the straightest answers we can offer to each.

items.question: Who can apply to IITG-TIC?
items.answer: Anyone with a working idea and an inherent zeal to build a venture — students, faculty, alumni and outside founders are all welcome. We particularly encourage applicants from the North-East.

items.question: What kind of ideas does the centre support?
items.answer: Technology-led ideas — deep tech, hardware, software platforms, embedded systems, knowledge-based products. The idea should have a credible path to becoming a commercially viable venture.

items.question: What support does the centre provide?
items.answer: Workspace inside the Technology Complex, technical assistance, business mentoring, network access, and — subject to availability — a soft-loan facility.

items.question: Is funding available?
items.answer: Yes. Soft-loan support is available for qualifying incubatees, and we work with funding partners including the Technology Development Board and Startup India for further capital.

items.question: Do I need to be affiliated with IIT Guwahati?
items.answer: No. While we have a strong link with the IITG community, we welcome founders from anywhere — particularly from across the North-East ecosystem.

items.question: How long is the incubation programme?
items.answer: Programme length varies with the venture. Some incubatees graduate inside a year; others stay through multi-year R&D arcs. The arrangement is shaped to fit the work.

items.question: How do I apply?
items.answer: Head to the Apply page and submit your idea. Our team will review it and reach out for a conversation if it looks like a fit.

hero.lede: Short writing from our team and incubatees — what we're seeing in applications, what we're learning from cohorts, and what the work actually looks like in practice.

posts.title: What we look for
posts.excerpt: A note from the programme team on the signals in an application that catch our attention — and the ones that don't.
posts.author: The IITG-TIC programme team

coverImage.alt: A whiteboard from a recent application review session.

body.text: Every application that lands in our inbox gets read by at least two people on the programme team. We don't have a rubric we tick down — we have a feeling we're chasing. Below is our best attempt to write it down.
The first thing we look for is specificity. Vague ideas with broad ambition are common; specific ideas with narrow ambition are rare. We back the second.

body.alt: A whiteboard from our last cohort review session.
body.caption: Most of our application reads start here — one whiteboard, two chairs.

body.text: Founder–problem fit

You don't need to be the world's expert on the problem, but you should be the person in the room who cares most about this particular problem — and has been thinking about it for longer than a quarter.
We look at the years of context behind an application. Not for credentials — for the slow conviction that comes from staying with a problem when the easier thing was to leave it.

body.caption: Application notes accumulate. We keep them across cohorts.

body.text: What won't work

This is the one most applications miss. If you can tell us five reasons your idea might fail and how you'd notice each one, we'll spend an hour with you on a call. Most applicants only tell us why it will work.
We're less interested in pitch decks than in the application body. Read what you've written out loud before you submit it. If a sentence sounds like a press release, change it.

posts.title: Hardware and soft loans
posts.excerpt: A short essay on funding deep-tech ideas in the North-East — and why patience is part of the work.
posts.author: IITG-TIC editorial

body.text: Software startups raise capital. Hardware startups raise capital, then raise more capital, then raise more capital again — usually with nothing visibly different to show for it between rounds. That gap is where the soft-loan facility lives.

Most hardware ventures coming through IITG-TIC need around eighteen months between a working prototype and a paying customer. That's not because the team is slow — it's because the supply chain, the certifications, the bill-of-materials engineering, and the field trials all stack.

body.caption: Iteration four of an enclosure that took six iterations to ship.

body.text: Patient by design
A soft loan is patient by design. It doesn't ask for an exit. It doesn't push you to ship before the product is ready. It buys the year and a half between knowing-it-works and knowing-it-sells.
We've had cohorts where the soft-loan facility was the only capital between pre-seed and revenue. It's not glamorous funding. It's the kind that lets you stop checking your bank balance every Friday.

body.alt: The TIC machine workshop on a quiet weekend.
body.caption: Most of the hard work happens here on the weekends — quietly.

body.text: If you're thinking about applying with a hardware idea: bring a credible plan for how the next eighteen months will look. You don't need to be right about every step. You need to have already walked yourself through them.

posts.title: Notes from the cohort
posts.excerpt: Three incubatees share what they learned by writing about their work as it happened — building in public.
posts.author: Aru, Priyanka and Rohan — current cohort

coverImage.alt: Cohort whiteboards at the end of Q1.

body.text: We asked three founders from the current cohort to write about what they learned by writing about their work as it happened. Building in public is a phrase that gets thrown around — these are notes from people who actually tried it.

body.alt: Our cohort whiteboards at the end of Q1.
body.caption: Every whiteboard becomes a draft of next quarter's plan.

body.text: Aru — hardware lead at a sensor startup

When I started writing weekly updates, I thought I was writing for our community. I wasn't. I was writing for myself. The act of explaining the week to a hypothetical reader is the act of finding out what I actually did.
Priyanka — founder of a data infrastructure company

Writing in public meant our customer pipeline filled before we had a finished product. People emailed us because they recognised their problem in our notes. We were not selling — we were just thinking out loud, and that was enough.

body.alt: A copy of Priyanka's printed customer logbook.
body.caption: A logbook compiled from the cold inbound that came from public notes.

body.text: Rohan — building in robotics
I almost stopped writing twice. Both times, something an investor said three weeks later traced back to one of those posts. The signal is delayed. You have to keep going past where it feels worth it.
We've put together the full essays from each of them in a separate publication. Mail us if you'd like a copy.

hero.lede: Our mentors aren't here to lecture — they're here to think with you. Each mentorship track pairs incubatees with senior practitioners who have done the work themselves.

tracks.bio: Senior engineers and researchers across hardware, software and embedded systems — there to sharpen the technical core of your idea.
Operators who have built and scaled ventures — there to challenge your market thinking, pricing and growth path.
Practitioners from manufacturing, energy, healthcare and IT — there to ground your work in the realities of your sector.
Patents, contracts, founder agreements — there when you need to protect the work or set things up cleanly.
Investors and finance leaders — there to help you raise, budget and read the numbers honestly.
Communicators who have positioned products for partners, press and customers — there to help you say what you do, clearly.

hero.lede: A home for new-age entrepreneurs and young minds to transform innovative ideas into viable business ventures — with mentorship, infrastructure, and a multidisciplinary push from IIT Guwahati and the wider North-East ecosystem.

sections.label: Who We Are
paragraphs: The Indian Institute of Technology Guwahati — Technology Incubation Centre (IITG-TIC) is a space for new-age entrepreneurs and young minds to transform their innovative ideas into viable business propositions. Our primary goal is to facilitate a platform where a budding entrepreneur can start a business venture with minimum risks.

IITG-TIC ensures that incubatees have access to technological assistance, generated through mentors with multidisciplinary expertise. We encourage young enthusiasts — those with creative pursuits and an inherent zeal to be entrepreneurs — to take advantage of this novel initiative.

callout.text: Curious about the people who keep this space alive? Come say hello to the team that powers it every day.
callout.label: Meet the TIC Team

sections.label: Our Mission
paragraphs: IITG-TIC is registered as a Society under the Registration of Societies Act XXI of 1860. Its goal is to encourage entrepreneurial initiatives amongst the faculty and alumni of the IITG community in particular — and other State or Central Government technical institutions of the North-East more broadly. It is an opportunity to explore and implement innovative ideas into commercially viable products through technology startup companies.

The centre facilitates interdisciplinary research with special emphasis on the development and innovation of high-growth, knowledge-based businesses — and nurtures indigenous products with innovative hardware and embedded designs.

callout.text: This mission only moves because of the mentors who walk alongside our founders. Take a moment to meet the people who carry it forward.
callout.label: Meet our Mentors

sections.label: Infrastructure & Support
paragraphs: Technical support, business mentoring, and a soft-loan facility — subject to availability — are the key services of this centre. Spreading across an area of approximately 4,000 square metres within the Technology Complex of IIT Guwahati, IITG-TIC has the adequate infrastructure for this endeavour.

Funds for developing basic infrastructure and the soft-loan facility are provided by the Department of Information Technology, Govt. of India. IITG-TIC is also one of the Business Incubators approved and recognised by the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Govt. of India. The Technology Development Board, under the Ministry of Science & Technology, has additionally approved grant assistance to IITG-TIC to support startup units.

callout.text: Wondering what working out of this space actually looks like? Take a closer look at our incubation programmes and the support we offer.
callout.label: Explore Incubation

sections.label: Governance
paragraphs: IITG-TIC has a seven-member Governing Body under the Chairmanship of the Director of IIT Guwahati. A Management Council directs and administers the smooth functioning of the centre. Currently, the Management Team of the IITG-TIC is led by a Chief Executive Officer.
